items.stem: Which TWO conditions must hold for a heat engine to achieve the Carnot efficiency? (Select TWO.)

options.text: All processes in the cycle are reversible
options.rationale: Correct: the Carnot limit requires reversible operation.

options.text: The engine operates between two fixed-temperature reservoirs
options.rationale: Correct: Carnot efficiency is defined by the two reservoir temperatures.

options.text: The working substance must be an ideal gas
options.rationale: Carnot efficiency is independent of the working substance.

options.text: The cold reservoir must be at absolute zero
options.rationale: That would require infinite resources and is unattainable.

items.explanation: Correct: the Carnot limit requires reversible operation.

items.stem: Why does the entropy of the universe increase when a hot object is placed in contact with a cold one?

options.text: The heat flow is irreversible, and the cold object gains more entropy than the hot one loses
options.rationale: Correct: dS = dQ/T is larger at the lower temperature, so total entropy rises.

options.text: Energy is destroyed in the transfer
options.rationale: Energy is conserved; entropy, not energy, increases.

options.text: The hot object gains entropy as it cools
options.rationale: The hot object loses entropy as it loses heat.

options.text: Entropy is conserved in all heat transfers
options.rationale: Entropy is conserved only in reversible processes.

items.explanation: Correct: dS = dQ/T is larger at the lower temperature, so total entropy rises.
